title: Regulation (EU) 2023/988 on general product safety, full text
publisher: EUR-Lex, Publications Office of the European Union
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Applies from 13 Dec 2024 (Art 52); Art 9 internal risk analysis, technical documentation kept 10 years, type, batch or serial number, name and postal and electronic address; Art 16 an economic operator established in the EU must be responsible; Art 19 information required in online offers; Art 20 accidents notified through the Safety Business Gateway; Art 36 recall notices headed "Product safety recall"; Art 37 remedy choice of at least two of repair, replacement or refund.

title: Product safety
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Describes the GPSR and Safety Gate, the EU rapid alert system for dangerous non-food products, with links to business obligations and online marketplace registration.

title: CE marking
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page last checked 17 Jul 2026). CE marking only for products under EU rules that require it (examples include toys, electrical equipment, PPE); steps from requirements to declaration of conformity; notified body number next to the mark where third-party assessment is required; at least 5 mm; documents kept 10 years; must not be used where no EU rule requires it.

title: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 on liability for defective products, full text
publisher: EUR-Lex, Publications Office of the European Union
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Art 4(1): product includes software, digital manufacturing files and raw materials; Art 8: when the manufacturer is outside the EU, the importer, authorised representative or fulfilment service provider can be liable; Art 21-22: old directive repealed with effect from 9 Dec 2026, still applying to products placed on the market before; national laws due by 9 Dec 2026.

title: Textile labelling
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page last checked 13 Jul 2026). Fibre composition label for products at least 80% textile fibres by weight; only fibre names in Annex I of the EU regulation; percentages in decreasing order; translated into the languages of each country of sale; non-textile parts of animal origin must be shown.

title: EU Customs Tariff (TARIC)
publisher: European Commission, Taxation and Customs Union
supports: Opened with WebFetch. TARIC holds EU tariff measures, preferences, trade defence duties and import restrictions; it does not include national VAT or excise.

title: Batteries
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries in force since 17 Aug 2023 and applying from 18 Feb 2024; covers portable and other battery categories across sustainability, safety, labelling, due diligence and end of life.

title: General Product Safety Regulations 2005
publisher: GOV.UK (Office for Product Safety and Standards)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 13 Dec 2024). The 2005 regulations require consumer products to be safe in normal or reasonably foreseeable use and apply in England, Scotland and Wales; in Northern Ireland they were superseded on 13 Dec 2024 by the EU GPSR.

title: Product safety for businesses: A to Z of industry guidance
publisher: GOV.UK (Office for Product Safety and Standards)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 2 Mar 2026). Product-specific guidance (electrical, radio, toys, cosmetics, furniture and more); general product safety applies where no specific regulation covers a product.

title: Product Recalls and Alerts
publisher: GOV.UK (Office for Product Safety and Standards)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 6 Oct 2026). OPSS publishes recalls, product safety reports and product safety alerts; a business that has placed an unsafe product on the market should notify its market surveillance authority.

title: Using the UKCA marking
publisher: GOV.UK (Office for Product Safety and Standards)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 21 Aug 2026). Great Britain continues to recognise CE marking; UK approved bodies are accredited by UKAS and certify only for UKCA; UKCA may go on a label or accompanying document until 11pm on 31 Dec 2027; marks at least 5 mm; manufacturer and importer name and postal address; instructions in English.

title: Placing manufactured goods on the market in Great Britain
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 17 May 2024). Covers about 19 product areas; on 24 Jan 2024 the government signalled continued CE recognition for a range of product regulations, and the 31 Dec 2024 end date was removed on 17 May 2024.

title: Register a design
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A new design (shape, configuration, decoration, pattern) can be registered in the UK; renew every 5 years up to 25 years; the functionality of a design cannot be registered.

title: Trade Tariff: look up commodity codes, duty and VAT rates
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Look up UK commodity codes, duty and VAT for imports and exports; gather product type, use, materials, production method and packaging first.

title: Business and Manufacturing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Hub linking testing and certification, CPSC-accepted labs, eFiling, the Regulatory Robot, small business resources, recall guidance, tracking labels and the online sellers' safety guide.

title: General Use Products Certification and Testing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A General Certificate of Conformity is issued by the importer (or US manufacturer) for general use products subject to a CPSC rule, ban, standard or regulation, based on a test of each product or a reasonable testing program; it accompanies each shipment; from 8 Jul 2026 importers of most regulated products must eFile certificate data.

title: Third Party Testing for Children's Products
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Children's products need testing by a CPSC-accepted third-party lab and a Children's Product Certificate; more than 600 labs accepted worldwide; material changes need retesting; periodic testing for continued production; eFiling from 8 Jul 2026.

title: Tracking Labels
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Children's products and their packaging carry permanent tracking information to the extent practicable: manufacturer or private labeler name, location and date of production, batch or run number.

title: CPSC-Accepted Laboratories
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Search tool for labs CPSC has accepted to perform specific tests for each children's product safety rule.

title: Duty to Report to the CPSC: Your Rights and Responsibilities
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Manufacturers, importers, distributors and retailers must report within 24 hours of obtaining reportable information about defects that could create a substantial product hazard, unreasonable risks of serious injury or death, or failure to meet a rule; up to 10 working days to investigate if unsure; "when in doubt, report"; failing to report can bring civil or criminal penalties.

title: Regulatory Robot: Safer Products Start Here
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A question-led tool for new small businesses to find which CPSC requirements may apply to one product; basic guidance and a starting point, run separately for each product.

title: Samsung Recalls Galaxy Note7 Smartphones Due to Serious Fire and Burn Hazards
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Recall of about 1 million units on 15 Sep 2016; battery could overheat and catch fire; 92 US reports of overheating including 26 burns and 55 property damage.

title: Samsung Expands Recall of Galaxy Note7 Smartphones Based on Additional Incidents with Replacement Phones
supports: Opened with WebFetch. On 13 Oct 2016 the recall grew to about 1.9 million units including replacement phones; 96 US reports of overheating, 13 burns and 47 property damage.

title: Threading Your Way Through the Labeling Requirements Under the Textile and Wool Acts
supports: Opened with WebFetch (guide dated July 2014). Labels show fibre content by generic name and percentage, country of origin and the company name or RN; care instructions are required by a separate FTC rule; country of origin inside the centre of the neck on garments with a neck; English required.

title: Determining Duty Rates
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last modified 25 Nov 2024). The HTSUS lists duty rates; classification depends on details such as materials and origin; the USITC tariff database gives an approximate rate; CBP makes the final determination; binding rulings can be requested.

title: Incoterms rules
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Incoterms 2020 is the most recent version, in force since 1 Jan 2020; eleven three-letter trade terms covering the tasks, costs and risks of delivery between seller and buyer; first published in 1936.

title: Incoterms 2020
supports: Opened with WebFetch. DPU is the renamed DAT, and under DPU the seller unloads; CIP now requires higher insurance cover (Institute Cargo Clauses A or similar) while CIF keeps clauses C as default; FCA allows an on-board bill of lading; CIF is for sea transport.

title: Solving Wall Thickness Issues in Molded Parts
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated). Keep wall thickness consistent; thick sections cause sink, voids and warp; example wall ranges by resin (for example ABS about 1.1 to 3.6 mm); at least 0.5 degrees of draft on vertical faces, 1 degree where advised and up to 2 degrees for deep features. One supplier's process guidance.

title: Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guidelines
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Flanges at least 4 times material thickness; features within about 4 times thickness of a bend may deform; bend angles held to plus or minus 1 degree; use the same bend radius throughout; tolerances grow across more bends. One supplier's process guidance.
